positions.title: Lead II Software Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on simulating physical boards with SystemC (C++) and Synopsys Virtualizer.

Work involved bug fixing existing virtual platforms as well as helping to bring new platforms to functional parity with the specified designs.

Worked on complex VDK blocks in Synopsys Virtualizer that simulated many different communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, I3C, etc) to simulate the behavior of the planned physical board.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Santa Barbara, California, United States · Remote
positions.description:
I work primarily developing c++ with some c for embedded devices. The firmware I develop runs on all actively supported Sonos players. I have done work on power management, led control, wifi networking, network topology between players and multi-threaded logging.

I develop in a linux environment for devices that run embedded linux.

positions.title: Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
Developed firmware for multiple devices including SAMD21, NRF52 and C8051 microprocessors.
Developed system-level apps for controlling and visualizing multiple novel devices.
Developed api systems for communicating with our devices.
Worked on the entire data pipeline for multiple devices from ADC acquisition in firmware to sending and receiving on a system-level app for display.
Developed algorithms for detecting various types of user input including gesture detection.
Worked on firmware utilizing IMU chips both on existing implementations and initial bring-up of a new chip.
Designed and implemented machine learning models for posture detection and non-linear sensor hysteresis.
Implemented webusb protocols to make devices compatible with web applications.
Worked with NodeJS and Electron to both handle web interfaces for devices as well as deploying stable apps locally.

positions.title: Hardware Engineer
positions.description:
Product was a phone-attached photo printer for iOS and android.

>Designed circuit schematics for a new product
>Tested and fixed hardware issues on EVT boards
>Evaluated and integrated new components for reduced cost and lead times.
>Rewrote SPI protocol to UART to accommodate new on-board CPU

Circuit design in Altium.
Firmware development for ARM9 and PIC32 chips in C.
Hand soldering was used to test POC or fix EVT boards.
